source: research/mcr-colistin-seed.json (the review's Table 1, as transcribed); frame assignments from research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md §5c–§5e
method: Assign every row whose denominator has been read against its primary to exactly one frame, pool inside the frame, and report the range across frames. Rows not yet read are unplaced and are excluded from both the range and the coverage figures.

frames.why_this_row_is_here: each N is a count of bacterial isolates put through a molecular screen, so n/N is a gene prevalence among screened isolates. Row 19's printed numerator disagrees with its own primary by 100 (49 vs 149, §5b) — the frame is still this one, the cell is the error. Rows 17 (a)–17 (k) are the eleven country slices of one laboratory's stored porcine isolates, PCR-screened for mcr-1 and mcr-2 (§2a, §3, §5f); eight of them were placed on 2026-11-21 22:50Z from the shared methods section rather than from a fresh read. Row 7 (Bangladesh, 305/1,200) is here because its N is a count of E. coli isolates put through a multiplex PCR for mcr-1..5 (§5j) — but it is a clustered N: twenty isolates per pooled farm sample, sixty samples, twenty farms, so the denominator is 1,200 isolates carrying about 60 independent sampling events.

frames.frame: isolates screened for a phenotype, genotyped only if positive
frames.why_this_row_is_here: Canada genotyped the 12 colistin-resistant isolates of 5,571 and nothing else, so 2/5,571 is a lower bound among isolates tested for phenotype, not a gene prevalence (§5d).

the Portugal row's 227 are enrolled hosts and its 12 are positive hosts; the study's 17 isolates and the isolation medium's own colistin (3.5 µg/mL) are not in either number (§5e). Argentina's 140 are rectal swabs from pigs on six farms and its 23 are mcr-1-positive colistin-resistant E. coli recovered from them, so 16.4% is host carriage, not an isolate prevalence — the abstract's co-resistance profile is printed on 23 (20/23, 11/23, 19/23, 14/23), which fixes the numerator as isolates and the denominator as animals (§5i). Placed 2026-11-23 on the read recorded there; the row is the frame's second member, not a ninth frame.
row 18's 128 are retail poultry products; row 5's 1,112 are samples from duck farms and the surrounding water and soil, with 360 isolates recovered from them (§5c, §5e).

frames.frame: one recovered isolate per positive sample
frames.why_this_row_is_here: 147 of 570 Italian meat samples yielded E. coli and one isolate per sample was tested; the primary's own gene figure is 3/147, one more than the row prints (§5e).
the Algerian 103 are colistin-selected mixed-species isolates from 40 environmental samples at 8 sites — not samples, not sites, not E. coli (§5e).
the Chinese 2,649 add raw meat samples, animal samples and inpatient samples into one N and one n, with per-frame positivity of 14.9%, 20.6% and 1.2% (§5d).

frames.frame: colistin-resistant isolates, genotyped for the gene
frames.why_this_row_is_here: Brazil's 490 are not the isolates whose phenotype was tested (that is frame 2's 5,571 for Canada) but the isolates that PASSED the colistin-resistance screen: all 490 were PCR-screened and 8 E. coli carried mcr-1.1, so 8/490 is the share of the hospital's colistin resistance that is mcr-mediated, not a gene prevalence among isolates. The same study gives 8/19 = 42.1% among its resistant E. coli and 8/7,852 = 0.102% among all Gram-negative bacilli (§5h).

range.bases: the 8 frame rates, not the 24 row rates
range.low_frame: isolates screened for a phenotype, genotyped only if positive

what_this_does_not_say: That the frame rates are comparable with each other. They are not: that is the finding.

That the unplaced rows could not move the range. They could — 15 of 38 rows have no frame, and the largest of them (China 1,611 row 2, Japan 684 row 12, South Africa 50 row 26) could widen or narrow it; Tunisia 676 is now read and deliberately unplaced, per §5g.
That any row here is a population prevalence. Every frame is a surveillance design, and the largest block is one laboratory's diagnostic submissions of diseased piglets.
